title: -all says /all/
parentNote: Today is the -all family: ball, wall, tall, small, and the word all itself. It is yesterday's sound with an l on the end, so say aw and then all one after the other and let your child hear that the front half has not changed. The slip to expect is the a going back to saying aah, so ball comes out to rhyme with pal — and that is a fair guess, because a followed by two l letters is exactly what your child has been reading as short a in words like fell and hill since day fourteen. The fix is to treat all as one chunk your eye picks up whole, the way it already picks up ing. Cover the first letter, read all, then uncover it and push the sounds together. This family has been locked since day one and it is a big one to hand over: ball and call and small are words a small child uses every day, and today is the first day they can read them.

activities.mouthCue: Start it with your jaw dropped for aw, then flick the tip of your tongue up behind your top teeth for the l.
activities.prompt: Three letters, one chunk. It is yesterday's sound with an l stuck on the end.
You met one of these yesterday. Find the new one, the one that ends with your tongue up.
Now the other way round. Find the one that is just the wide open sound, with nothing after it.
Two parts, not four. Do not sound out the a and the two l letters on their own.
Two sounds at the front of this one, and they run into each other. Say them both: s, m.
The long one. Two teams in it. Sound out snow, then sound out ball, then push them together.
This one is the whole chunk on its own, with nothing in front of it.
All three start and end the same. The middle is where the work is.
All three end the same. Everything you need is in the very first sound.
This one is hard. Listen to the front first, and then to the middle.

activities.text: The ball did go up past the tall wall and did land in the next yard.
Meg said, "I can not get up that wall," and so I did lift her up.
"Call Dad!" said Mum, and I did run and yell up the hall.
All the buns did fall off the dish and did land on the mat.

activities.title: The ball and the tall wall
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Meg did kick the ball, and up it did go, up and up, and then it did fall in the next yard.
That wall is the tallest wall on the street, and we can not see past it.
I said, "Do you want to go and ask?" and Meg said the man in that yard is cross.
So we did call and call, and all we did get back is a big deep bark.
Meg did stand up on a pot to peep past the wall, and the pot did crack.
Off she did fall, and she did sit on the grass and rub her leg.
Then a black nose did poke out at a gap in the wall.
It is the dog. It did poke the ball out to us with its nose, and then it did sit still.
Meg said, "That dog is not cross at all!" and she did pat its nose.
Then the man did call out, "Do not kick it so hard next time!" and he did grin.
So we did sit next to the wall, and the small dog did peep out at us all day.
